note.text: Utility is the satisfaction a consumer obtains from consuming a good or service. It is subjective: people can value the same item differently. Total utility is satisfaction from all units consumed in a stated situation. Marginal utility is the change in total utility from an additional unit. Diminishing marginal utility means successive units add less satisfaction, other conditions held constant. Falling marginal utility need not mean falling total utility while each additional gain remains positive.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Utility is the satisfaction a consumer obtains from consuming a good or service. It is subjective: people can value the same item differently. Total utility is satisfaction from all units consumed in a stated situation. Marginal utility is the change in total utility from an additional unit. Diminishing marginal utility means successive units add less satisfaction, other conditions held constant. Falling marginal utility need not mean falling total utility while each additional gain remains positive.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: After walking in warm weather, Ayuk may value the first cup of water highly. A later cup can add less satisfaction. In a classroom numerical illustration, utility units are assumed, not scientifically measured happiness. They should not be used to claim that one person's satisfaction is objectively comparable with another's.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Keep total and additional satisfaction separate. Subtract consecutive total-utility values to calculate marginal utility for that increment. Check whether the increment is positive, zero or negative before stating how total utility changes. Hold the consumer and circumstances fixed when discussing diminishing marginal utility.

questions.prompt: In an assumed classroom utility table, total utility rises from {before} to {before+gain} units after one extra item. Find marginal utility.

misconceptions.explain: You reported the new total rather than the extra satisfaction.
Subtract the previous total; adding totals counts earlier satisfaction again.

solution: Marginal utility = new total − previous total.
